mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 900K units, indicating robust demand, boosts consumer discretionary spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and consumer spending
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when HOUST surpasses 900K units.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as investors seek higher yields.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 1.5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment (UNRATE) drops below 5% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 200K in a month, a tightening labor market drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, as firms invest in growth.
failure_condition: SPX returns over 60d are not significantly higher (t-test p > 0.1) when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) growth above 2% YoY signals increased economic activity, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as firms benefit from rising demand.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC falls below 0.01 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) exceeding $440B indicates strong consumer spending, boosting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, as retail and consumer discretionary sectors benefit.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of instances when RSAFS surpasses $440B.

mechanism_narrative: A 25bps increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) within a month signals monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as higher borrowing costs reduce investment.
failure_condition: SPX returns over 20d are not significantly lower (t-test p > 0.05) following a 25bps rate hike.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises by more than 0.5% in two months and payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth slows to under 100K, a weakening labor market drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, as firms reduce investment.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.5% in 2 months and PAYEMS growth < 100K
failure_condition: SPX returns over 60d are not significantly lower (t-test p > 0.1) when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: GDP (GDPC1) growth below 2% YoY indicates sluggish economic activity, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as firms face reduced demand.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains above 0.04 over any 1.5-year rolling window.
